label: copy phase: current and next output both from {n,h,p,j,f,u,2,1,(r)}
explanation: Fires almost entirely in the copy phase (92% of activation mass), mostly in the middle of recall (recall_idx 3-4, 2-3 outputs left). It is driven by WHICH tokens are being recalled: the current output out_tok (n 10x lift, h 9x, p 9x, j 6.5x, then f/2/u/1 at about 3-4x) and the next output next_out (h 10x, f 7x, n 6x, p 5x, r/2/1/u at about 3-4x). The strongest activations come when both the current and the next output are from this set, e.g. outputting n then p, or u then h. The input token adds a weaker effect (t 3.8x, y 2.9x). The predicate (copy phase, current output and next output both in the set) gets dev P=0.23 R=0.58 F1=0.33 mass recall 0.65. Precision is low: even on its best token pairs the unit is active only about 10-40% of the time, so it looks like a graded sum of per-token contributions from the upcoming outputs rather than a clean binary condition. Rarely fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, and never at t<2. Does not depend on L, digit count, or first token.
